transcript.text: Samsung WW90T534DAW keeps coming up with 4C after a couple of minutes. Drum is dry. Any ideas before I call someone out?

The 4C code on Samsung washing machines indicates a water supply issue—the machine isn't getting enough water to start properly. Since the drum is dry when the error appears, this suggests the problem is with the water entering the machine. Before you call an engineer, there are two simple checks that resolve most of these cases: 1. Check the inlet mesh filter: Over time, grit or limescale can block the small mesh filter where the fill hose connects to the back of the machine. This restricts flow and triggers 4C.
2. Check your water supply: Ensure the tap the hose is connected to is fully open, and check that the hose behind the machine isn't kinked or crushed against the wall. Could you please check the inlet mesh filter as described above? Let me know if it was blocked or clean.
[Helpful to see: image "Where the fill-hose mesh filter is" — A small mesh filter sits inside the fill-hose connector at the tap/valve end and catches grit. Turn the tap off, unscrew the hose and rinse the mesh. Typical layout — your machine may differ.]
Tap was already fully open and the hose isn't kinked. I'll turn it off and check the mesh filter now.

That sounds like a good plan. The inlet mesh filter is very commonly the culprit for 4C codes because even a small amount of limescale or sand can stop enough water from entering to satisfy the machine's sensors. Once you've checked it, let me know exactly what you found:
1. If it was blocked: clean it under running water and try again.
2. If it was clean: we'll need to check if your home's water pressure is sufficient for the machine (sometimes a separate tap valve isn't fully open or the hose is restricted). Please tell me what you see when you pull the filter out.
Checked it. The mesh filter was clogged with grey grit and limescale bits. Cleaning it now and will retry.

That sounds like exactly what was causing the issue. The grit and limescale were restricting the water flow enough to trigger the error. Please run a short wash programme (like Cotton 40°) and let me know if it fills normally or if the 4C code comes back. If it still shows 4C despite the filter being clean, we'll need to check if your home's water pressure is sufficient for the machine. This can happen if the tap valve itself isn't fully opening or if there's a restriction in the hose before it reaches the machine.
Cleaned the filter and reran it. It fills normally now and the 4C has gone.

That is excellent news. It was most likely the grit and limescale in that inlet filter restricting the water flow enough to trigger the 4C code. To help prevent this from happening again, it is a good idea to check that mesh filter every couple of years or if you notice the fill time getting slower. If your area has hard water, descaling your machine occasionally can also help reduce buildup. Is there anything else I can help you with regarding your washing machine?
